Mounting inflation concerns and geopolitical tensions that have driven oil prices higher continue to weigh on the long end of the curve. Together those forces have kept term premia elevated and left investors asking, just how far can the 10-year can still run before year-end?

Prediction-market traders on Polymarket are assigning a 78% chance the yield tags 5.2% before 2027. Odds then decline in steps: 63% that it reaches 5.3%, 45% for 5.4%, 30% for 5.5%, 8% for 5.7%, and 6% that it hits 6%. The pricing implies markets see a further move through 5.2% as the base case, with progressively lower probability of more extreme prints.

Whether those higher thresholds are tested will depend on incoming inflation data, energy prices, and the Federal Reserve’s response. For now, the 10-year sits at its most expensive level in nearly two decades, and the market is openly debating how much further the backup can go.

title: Just how high will the U.S. 10-year yield rise by year-end?
